title: Money Matters
goals: Compare prices, products and stores with comparatives (cheaper than, more expensive than, as ... as).
Say if something is too expensive or if you have enough money with too and enough.
Use someone, anything, nobody and other indefinite pronouns correctly.
Talk about a budget: income, expenses and savings.
Shop smart: ask about prices, discounts, receipts and returns.
Read a pay stub and understand gross pay, net pay and deductions.
Write a short recommendation of a product or a store.

learn.title: Comparatives
learn.html:
We use comparatives to say how two things or people are different. We usually use than after the comparative.

Type of adjectiveRuleExample
Short (one syllable)adjective + -erThis phone is cheaper than that one.
Ends in -y-y becomes -ierOnline shopping is easier than going to the mall.
Long (two or more syllables)more + adjectiveThis laptop is more expensive than my old one.
Irregulargood - better; bad - worse; far - fartherThe prices here are better than the prices there.
Same levelas + adjective + asMy phone is as expensive as yours.
Lessless + adjective / less + uncountable nounI spend less money than my brother.
  • Use much or a lot before a comparative to make it stronger: much cheaper, a lot more expensive.
  • With short adjectives that end in one vowel and one consonant, double the last letter: big - bigger.

watch.wrong: This bag is more cheap than that one.
watch.right: This bag is cheaper than that one.
watch.why: Short adjectives take -er. Do not use more with them.

watch.wrong: The bus is cheaper that the taxi.
watch.right: The bus is cheaper than the taxi.
watch.why: After a comparative, use than, not that.

watch.wrong: This TV is gooder than my old one.
watch.right: This TV is better than my old one.
watch.why: Good has an irregular comparative: better.

watch.wrong: She earns more as her sister.
watch.right: She earns more than her sister.
watch.why: Use than after more. Use as only in as ... as.

learn.title: too and enough
learn.html:
Too means more than we want or need. Enough means the right amount. Their position in the sentence is different.

StructureExampleMeaning
too + adjectiveThe jacket is too expensive.It costs more than I can pay.
too much + uncountable nounI spend too much money on food.More money than is good.
too many + plural nounThere are too many people in the store.More people than we want.
adjective + enoughThe shoes are big enough.The size is right.
enough + nounI don't have enough money.I need more money.
too / enough + for + personIt is too small for me.It does not fit me.
too / enough + to + verbI'm not rich enough to buy a house.I can't buy it.

Too is negative: it shows a problem. Very is only a strong word: This phone is very good (no problem) but This phone is too expensive (problem).

watch.why: With an adjective, enough goes after the adjective.

watch.wrong: I spend too many money on clothes.
watch.right: I spend too much money on clothes.
watch.why: Money is uncountable: too much, not too many.

watch.wrong: I don't have enough of money.
watch.why: Do not use of between enough and a noun.

watch.wrong: This phone is very expensive to buy it.
watch.right: This phone is too expensive to buy.
watch.why: Use too + adjective + to + verb. Do not repeat the object.

learn.title: Indefinite pronouns: someone, anything, nobody
learn.html:
We use indefinite pronouns when we don't say exactly which person, thing or place.

Some-Any-No-Every-
Peoplesomeone / somebodyanyone / anybodyno one / nobodyeveryone / everybody
Thingssomethinganythingnothingeverything
Placessomewhereanywherenowhereeverywhere
  • some- in positive sentences and in offers: Someone called you. Would you like something to drink?
  • any- in questions and negative sentences: Is there anything cheaper? I don't have anything.
  • no- already has a negative meaning. Use it with a positive verb: Nobody knows the price.
  • These pronouns are singular, so the verb is singular: Everybody is here.
  • Add an adjective after the pronoun: something cheaper, anything interesting.

watch.wrong: I don't have nothing in my wallet.
watch.right: I don't have anything in my wallet. / I have nothing in my wallet.
watch.why: Use only one negative in a sentence.
Nobody is already negative and takes a singular verb.

watch.wrong: Everybody are happy with the discount.
watch.right: Everybody is happy with the discount.

watch.wrong: Is there anything cheap than this?
watch.right: Is there anything cheaper than this?
watch.why: To compare, use the comparative after the pronoun.

learn.title: Useful expressions
learn.html:
• Let's make a budget. / We need to spend less. — planning money with someone.
  • What is our monthly income? / How much is our rent? — talking about numbers in a budget.
  • Can we afford it? / It's too expensive for us. — deciding if you can buy something.
  • Is that enough? / That's not enough. — checking an amount.
  • How much does this cost? / How much is it? — asking a price.
  • Is there a discount? / Do you have anything cheaper? — looking for a better price.
  • Can I pay by card? / Can I have the receipt, please? — paying in a store.
  • I'd like to return this. / Can I get a refund? — returning a product.
  • I recommend it. / It's worth the money. — recommending a product or a store.

write.prompt: Write a recommendation of a product or a store (120 to 160 words). Say what it is, why it is good, how it compares with other options (cheaper than, better than), what is not perfect (too..., not ... enough), and who you recommend it to. Opening: I want to recommend...
checklist: At least two comparatives with than
One sentence with too and one with enough
A clear recommendation at the end
Money and shopping vocabulary (price, discount, budget...)
write.model: I want to recommend Casa Verde, a small grocery store near my house in Guadalajara. It is not the biggest store in the neighborhood, but it is better than the supermarket for fresh food. The fruit and vegetables are fresher, and the prices are lower than in the big stores. Nobody there is rude: the owner always says hello and helps you find what you need. The store is small, so it is too crowded on Saturdays, and I usually go on weekday mornings. There is also something special: you can ask for a discount if you buy a lot of vegetables. I think it is the cheapest place for healthy food in my area. Is there anything I don't like? The store closes early, at 7 p.m., which is not late enough for people who work. Overall, I strongly recommend it, especially for families who want to save money.

write.prompt: Write a short message to a friend (80 to 120 words). You want to buy something (a phone, a bike, a laptop) and you need advice. Compare two options, say what is too expensive or not good enough, and ask a question with anything or someone.
checklist: Two options compared with a comparative
One sentence with too and one with enough
A question with anything, someone or anyone
write.model: Hi Sofia! I'm looking for a new phone, and I need your advice. My budget is not very high, so I can't buy something too expensive. I saw two models online. The first one is cheaper, but its camera isn't good enough for photos. The second one is more expensive and has a better battery. Does anyone you know have the second model? Is there anything I should check before I buy it? Please tell me what you think. Maybe we can go to the store together on Saturday and compare the prices. Thanks! Marco

reading.title: Smart Shopping for a New Laptop
reading.intro: Read about Marta's laptop and answer.
paragraphs: Last month, Marta decided to buy a new laptop for her studies. Her old computer was too slow, and it didn't have enough memory for her programs. She didn't have a lot of money, so she made a budget first. She wrote down her income and her fixed expenses, and she saw that she could spend about 9,000 pesos.

Marta started shopping online. At first, everything looked cheap and exciting. One laptop was cheaper than the others, but the reviews were bad: people said the battery was too weak and the screen was darker than in the photos. Another laptop was more expensive, but it was faster and lighter. It cost 11,500 pesos, which was too much for her budget.

Then Marta asked her cousin Ivan for help. "Nobody should buy the first thing they see," he said. "Compare prices in three different stores. Look for a discount, but also check the delivery cost and the warranty." Marta found something interesting: a store near her home sold the same laptop as the website, and it was 800 pesos cheaper because of a weekend sale.

She also learned that the best price is not always the best deal. A very cheap laptop with no warranty can be more expensive in the end if it breaks after six months. Marta read the return policy carefully. She wanted to be sure that someone could help her if there was a problem.

Finally, she bought a laptop for 8,700 pesos. It is not the newest model, but it is fast enough for her classes, and it is lighter than her old one. She paid with her debit card, kept the receipt, and put it in a folder. Now she is saving a little money every month, and she has an emergency fund. "Smart shopping takes more time," she says, "but it is much cheaper than a mistake."

listening.title: Making a family budget
listening.intro: Listen to a couple who make a budget. You can repeat it.

lines.text: Luis, we need to make a budget. We spend more money every month.
You're right. Our rent is higher than last year, and food is more expensive too.
Let's write down our income first. I earn 14,000 pesos, and you earn 12,500.
So we have 26,500 pesos a month. Now the fixed expenses: rent, electricity, internet and the bus.
Rent is 9,000. Electricity is not very high, only 600. Internet is 500.
What about entertainment? Streaming, restaurants, movies. We spend too much there.
I agree. Nobody needs three streaming accounts. We can cancel two of them.
Good idea. And I want to save something every month. Is 3,000 pesos enough?
It's not enough for a vacation, but it's a good start. Let's try 4,000.
Okay. Is there anything else we forgot?
Yes, the gym. Nobody goes there anymore. It's too expensive for what we use.
Then we can cancel it too. Let's put everything in a spreadsheet tonight.
